title: Monetary policy
examples: How does the central bank actually change interest rates?
What is the difference between raising and lowering interest rates?
Can quantitative easing be used when interest rates are already zero?

explain.say: Today we are learning about monetary policy tools. These tools help control the money supply in an economy.

items: Tools include interest rates and QE

explain.say: Interest rates are the cost of borrowing money. Central banks influence these rates to manage inflation.
When the central bank raises rates, borrowing becomes more expensive. This slows down spending and cools inflation.
The transmission mechanism explains how policy changes affect the real economy. It is a chain reaction of effects.
Quantitative easing involves buying assets to increase money supply. This supports lending when rates are near zero.
In everyday life, mortgage rates show this policy in action. Lower rates make buying a house more affordable for people.

faq.q: What is the primary goal of monetary policy?
faq.a: The main goal is usually to maintain price stability and support maximum sustainable employment. It aims to keep the economy running smoothly.
asks: Why do central banks manage money?
What is the central bank trying to achieve?

faq.q: If the central bank raises interest rates, what happens to my car loan?
faq.a: Your bank will likely increase the interest rate on your loan. This means your monthly repayments will become more expensive for you.
asks: How does rate hikes affect loans?
Will my borrowing cost go up?

faq.a: It is when a central bank buys large amounts of assets, like government bonds. This injects money into the financial system to keep credit flowing.
asks: What does QE mean for banks?
Is QE the same as printing money?

faq.q: Does monetary policy affect all types of borrowing?
faq.a: It affects almost all forms of credit, including mortgages, business loans, and credit card debt. The cost of money rises or falls generally.
asks: Does it affect business loans too?
Is it only for big banks?

faq.q: How long does it take for policy changes to affect me?
faq.a: The transmission mechanism takes time. Changes in rates might take several months before they significantly impact consumer spending or inflation.
asks: How quickly do rates change things?

facts: Central banks use monetary policy to manage inflation and economic growth.
Raising interest rates generally aims to slow down an overheating economy and curb inflation.
Quantitative easing involves the central bank purchasing financial assets from commercial banks.
The transmission mechanism describes the path from policy action to real economic outcomes.

quiz.say: If the central bank wants to slow down rapid price increases, what action is most likely?
quiz.why: Higher rates increase borrowing costs, which reduces overall demand and helps cool down inflation.

wrong.0: QE increases money supply, which tends to boost demand and inflation.
wrong.1: This is not the primary tool; rate changes are the mechanism used to control supply.
wrong.3: This increases borrowing, which usually stimulates demand and can worsen inflation.

quiz.say: When the central bank buys government bonds, what is the direct effect?

options.show: Causing an immediate fall in prices
options.say: Causing an immediate fall in prices

quiz.why: Buying assets injects money into the banking system, increasing the overall money supply.

wrong.1: This would happen if the central bank sold assets into the open market.
wrong.2: QE itself is a tool to keep rates low, not a direct rate hike.
wrong.3: The effect on prices is indirect and takes time through the transmission mechanism.

quiz.say: If the central bank lowers rates to encourage spending, what is the immediate expected impact on consumers?

options.show: A reduction in the central bank's power
options.say: A reduction in the central bank's power

quiz.why: Lower rates reduce the cost of taking out loans, making big purchases like cars or houses more affordable.

wrong.0: The central bank's power remains, but its tools are used to influence the economy.
wrong.2: Wages are determined by labor supply and demand, not directly by monetary policy.
wrong.3: Lowering rates stimulates demand, which can sometimes contribute to future inflation.
